title: Causal Consequence Calibration for Quantized World Action Models
title_zh: 量化 World Action Models 的因果后果校准
hook: At a matched high-precision-unit budget, the candidate predicts that the rank correlation between local PTQ discrepancy and paired one-step closed-loop consequence will drop specifically on contact-transition states, while consequence-ranked protection will reduce contact-sensitive task failures relative to local-score ranking. The surprising result is the regime split, not a claim that local numerical error is useless everywhere. C_r is not task loss, the physical consequence of executing the full action chunk or a replan horizon, a marginal effect in the jointly low-bit deployment, or a bytes/latency objective; any reduction in held-out task failures is only an empirical predictive test of transfer from this one-control-transition proxy.
abstract_draft: Post-training quantization (PTQ) of a coupled future-video/action world action model (WAM) needs a site-selection signal that reflects action-mediated contact consequences, not merely local numerical discrepancy. The bottleneck is that a local score can be poorly aligned with state-specific transitions: QuantWAMs (arxiv:2607.28405v1) already covers joint video/action sensitivity and closed-loop protection scheduling, while QuantWM (arxiv:2602.02110v1) covers weight/activation sensitivity and long-horizon latent planning, but neither supplies the bounded single-site operator proposed here. One-Transition Consequence PTQ (OTC-PTQ) perturbs one weight/activation site while all other target sites remain FP16, compares paired full action chunks, executes only the first action, and combines the next-observation discrepancy into C_r. The contribution is this one-control-transition proxy for ranking protection sites under a matched high-precision-unit budget; C_r is not task loss, a full-horizon or replan marginal, a jointly-low-bit marginal, or a bytes/latency objective. The falsification prediction is a contact-transition-specific divergence from local-score ranking, transfer to fewer contact-sensitive held-out failures and lower next-observation deviation, and disappearance of the advantage after permuting C_r. A negative result rejects the transfer claim; a positive result supports only this bounded predictive use.

motivation.problem_framing:
For a coupled future-video/action WAM, calibration is not only about reproducing local tensors: a numerical intervention can change the predicted action chunk and, after the first action is executed, the next simulator observation. The concrete bottleneck is selecting which weight/activation sites should remain high precision when a local PTQ discrepancy does not consistently identify contact-transition consequences. The candidate therefore treats the full action chunk as an intermediate object and the one resulting control transition as the measurable boundary.

QuantWAMs (arxiv:2607.28405v1) already covers joint video/action sensitivity and closed-loop protection scheduling, and QuantWM (arxiv:2602.02110v1) covers weight/activation sensitivity with long-horizon latent planning. Earlier task-consequence work—VAML, Model Advantage / Value-Aware Model Learning, and Deep Task-Based Quantization—establishes that downstream consequence can guide targeting; SQIL establishes mission-critical-state protection through saliency-weighted QAT and action distillation. The gap is consequently narrower: OTC-PTQ asks whether a single numerical W/A intervention, with every other target site at FP16, can provide a reproducible one-control-transition proxy without claiming any of those broader principles as new.
motivation.why_now: The current Phase 0 frontier makes the boundary testable: QuantWAMs (arxiv:2607.28405v1) makes coupled video/action sensitivity and closed-loop protection explicit, QuantWM (arxiv:2602.02110v1) supplies a distinct latent rollout/planning sensitivity branch, and Fast-WAM (semanticscholar:b5be12ccbb037be57a1dbc03fbd43d379170055f) provides the named idm feasibility path without supplying a numerical PTQ consequence signal. Together with the stated RoboTwin 2.0/LIBERO manipulation split and Fast-WAM-only staged validation budget, this supports a small one-transition diagnostic now, provided the exact Optional IDM checkpoint identity is fixed in the pre-run manifest.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: QuantWAMs measures joint video/action empirical-Fisher cross terms across block and denoising-step granularity and repairs fixed-count closed-loop protection schedules.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not define the candidate's single-site W/A FP16-background intervention with paired full-action-chunk and next-observation C_r from one executed control transition.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Its object is joint sensitivity and schedule repair, so it does not supply this one-site simulator counterfactual and one-transition numerical proxy.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: QuantWM studies weight/activation PTQ sensitivity and long-horizon error in a DINO-WM latent planning setting.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not instantiate a manipulation WAM coupled future-video/action denoiser with a single-site FP16-background intervention and C_r from full-chunk/next-observation discrepancy.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Its latent rollout/planning estimand is different, leaving the coupled action-mediated transition measurement unspecified.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: Fast-WAM isolates video co-training from explicit future imagination and provides the named idm feasibility path for this branch.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not provide a numerical PTQ consequence signal for one-site W/A protection allocation.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: The missing mechanism is a paired simulator counterfactual that links a perturbed action chunk to the next observation after only the first action is executed.

motivation.what_changes_when_gap_closes: If the gap closes, the field gains a bounded diagnostic for identifying when local PTQ discrepancy stops predicting one-control-transition consequence on contact states, complementing QuantWAMs' closed-loop protection branch and QuantWM's latent-planning sensitivity branch. It also becomes possible to test whether a C_r-ranked schedule transfers to held-out contact-sensitive failures and next-observation deviation under the same precision budget, with permutation separating the consequence association from the quantizer and site-count controls. This would not establish task-loss identity, a full-horizon/replan marginal, joint-low-bit optimality, or a bytes/latency objective.

core_claim: In a coupled future-video/action WAM, ranking single-site W/A PTQ interventions by C_r—the paired full-action-chunk and next-observation discrepancy after only the first action is executed—will predict contact-transition sensitivity better than local discrepancy at a matched protection budget, without making C_r a task-loss or full-horizon marginal.

sub_claims.statement: With all other target sites at FP16, a single numerical W/A intervention yields a paired one-control-transition C_r built from full-action-chunk discrepancy and next-observation pixel L1.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Defines the bounded action-mediated consequence proxy that replaces an unqualified local-score target.

sub_claims.statement: The rank correlation between local discrepancy and C_r will diverge specifically on contact-transition states rather than uniformly across the calibration registry.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Tests the state-conditional structure of the quantization bottleneck.

sub_claims.statement: A C_r-ranked protection schedule will reduce contact-sensitive held-out task failures and next-observation deviation relative to matched local-score ranking, while permuting C_r across sites will remove that advantage.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Tests transfer from the one-control-transition proxy to downstream behavior without equating the proxy with task loss.

key_equations.description: Apply the low-bit operator only at numerical site r and keep every other target site at FP16.
key_equations.description_zh: 只在 numerical site r 应用 low-bit operator，其余目标 site 保持 FP16。

key_equations.latex: d_a(j,r)=\frac{\operatorname{MSE}(\mathbf a_{jr},\mathbf a_{j0})}{\max(\sigma_a^2,\epsilon_a^2)},\quad d_o(j,r)=\frac{\operatorname{mean}_{\mathrm{pixel}}\left|\mathbf o_{(j+1)r}-\mathbf o_{(j+1)0}\right|}{\max(\sigma_o,\epsilon_o)},\quad C_r=\operatorname{mean}_{j\in D_{\mathrm{cal}}}\left(\lambda_a d_a(j,r)+\lambda_o d_o(j,r)\right)
key_equations.description: Define d_a as the full-action-chunk MSE divided by max(sigma_a^2, epsilon_a^2), and d_o as the mean per-pixel absolute next-observation difference divided by max(sigma_o, epsilon_o). Use epsilon_a=epsilon_o=1e-3 in normalized units, lambda_a=lambda_o=1 by default with the preregistered sensitivity sweeps, and aggregate C_r as the episode mean with bootstrap intervals over complete episodes.
key_equations.description_zh: d_a 是完整 action chunk 的 MSE 除以 max(sigma_a^2, epsilon_a^2)，d_o 是 next observation 的 per-pixel 绝对差除以 max(sigma_o, epsilon_o)。在 normalized units 中使用 epsilon_a=epsilon_o=1e-3，默认 lambda_a=lambda_o=1 并执行预注册 sensitivity sweeps；C_r 按 episode mean 聚合，并在完整 episode 上计算 bootstrap intervals。

key_equations.description: Select the top B_site numerical sites by C_r; the site count is not a bytes or latency target.
key_equations.description_zh: 按 C_r 选择前 B_site 个 numerical site；site count 不等同于 bytes 或 latency 目标。

key_equations.description: Compare local-score versus C_r rank correlation by state subset, with the predicted divergence concentrated on contact-transition states.

method_flow.high_level_pipeline: First freeze an exact pre-run manifest and make controller, RNG, history, and cache restoration executable for replayable calibration states. For each state, quantize one W/A site while every other target site remains FP16, generate paired full action chunks, execute only the first action, and compute the normalized d_a and d_o terms to obtain the episode-mean C_r. Rank sites by C_r and by local discrepancy under B_site, with B equivalent to B_site, then compare their bounded transfer on the stated held-out manipulation split. The contact-transition subset, C_r permutation, and oracle simulator-state branch distinguish a consequence signal from local-score correlation or calibration noise.

steps.title: Freeze a replayable calibration state
steps.what_changes: Before any paired measurement, freeze the calibration registry and pre-run manifest, including the exact Fast-WAM checkpoint identity and the idm configuration; make controller, RNG, history, and cache restoration executable. For the Optional IDM path, an absent or mismatched exact checkpoint identity is a halt condition.
steps.why_this_step: A paired consequence is interpretable only when both branches start from the same recoverable state; this preserves the version boundary instead of treating an unverified checkpoint as interchangeable.
steps.input: Fast-WAM calibration states, the FP16 reference, and the pre-run manifest
steps.output: Replayable calibration records with verified controller, RNG, history, and cache restoration

steps.title: Apply a single-site W/A intervention
steps.what_changes: For each numerical weight or activation site r, apply the chosen low-bit operator only at r and keep every other target site at FP16, yielding a paired branch for the same calibration record.
steps.why_this_step: This isolates the candidate's bounded site intervention and avoids treating joint coupling, joint-low-bit marginal effects, or joint optimality as new claims.
steps.input: A replayable FP16 calibration record and the registered W/A site set
steps.output: A single-site low-bit branch paired with the FP16 reference branch

steps.title: Measure one-transition consequence
steps.what_changes: Run both branches from matched restored states to produce complete action chunks, then execute only the first action and record the immediate next observation. For episode j and site r, define d_a(j,r) as the full-action-chunk MSE divided by max(sigma_a^2, epsilon_a^2), where sigma_a^2 is the population variance over all scalar coordinates of FP16 full action chunks in D_cal. Define d_o(j,r) as the mean per-pixel absolute next-observation difference divided by max(sigma_o, epsilon_o), where sigma_o is the calibration mean per-pixel standard deviation. Use epsilon_a=epsilon_o=1e-3 in normalized units, lambda_a=lambda_o=1 by default with a preregistered lambda_a/lambda_o sweep over {0.5,1,2}, and aggregate C_r as the episode mean with bootstrap intervals over complete episodes. Also define the open-loop local surrogate L_jr as the mean squared difference over all elements of the paired hook outputs and L_r as its episode mean.
steps.why_this_step: This defines a one-control-transition proxy for action-mediated consequence while explicitly avoiding identity with task loss, a full-horizon/replan marginal, or a jointly-low-bit marginal.
steps.input: The paired single-site and FP16 branches plus the restored simulator state
steps.output: Sitewise C_r values paired with local discrepancy values

steps.title: Allocate protection at a matched budget
steps.what_changes: Rank sites by C_r and by local discrepancy separately. Define B_site, with B equivalent to B_site everywhere in this method, as the nonnegative integer high-precision-site count recorded by the matched local-fidelity baseline in the preregistered run manifest; upgrade exactly the top-B_site sites and leave all other sites at b_lo. The primary comparison is a site-count budget only, with ties resolved by registry order; record persistent weight bytes, peak live activation workspace, scale/copy overhead, and measured latency separately in a deployment-cost ledger.
steps.why_this_step: The comparison tests whether the proxy changes protection choices at a matched precision budget, rather than introducing a storage or runtime objective.
steps.output: Matched C_r-ranked and local-score-ranked protection schedules

steps.title: Run the bounded transfer and permutation check
steps.what_changes: On the exact manifest, run idm with sigma_shift_FW=1.0 and infer_action on the stated small held-out RoboTwin 2.0/LIBERO manipulation split using the same b_lo and B; compare contact-sensitive task failures and next-observation deviation for the two schedules, then permute C_r across the site registry and use the stated oracle simulator-state branch as a positive control.
steps.why_this_step: The contact-transition subset and permutation are load-bearing mechanism tests: the candidate predicts ranking divergence and transfer for the real C_r association, with its advantage disappearing after permutation; the oracle branch checks calibration noise.
steps.input: Verified paired calibration signals, matched schedules, the exact manifest, and the held-out manipulation split
steps.output: A bounded transfer result and a mechanism-distinguisher result

method_flow.design_reasoning_echo: The design deliberately narrows the estimand. A single-site FP16-background intervention keeps the comparison interpretable when joint coupling and joint-low-bit marginals are already covered by prior work; the paired simulator counterfactual adds an action-mediated consequence signal that a local score does not provide. Executing only the first action keeps the claim at one control transition instead of silently becoming a full-horizon or replan marginal. Combining normalized full-action-chunk MSE d_a with normalized next-observation pixel L1 d_o, using lambda_a=lambda_o=1 by default and an episode-mean C_r, preserves the stated numerical operator. The allocation uses B_site with B equivalent to B_site and a separate deployment-cost ledger, not bytes or latency as the protection budget. Exact checkpoint identity plus executable controller/RNG/history/cache restoration protects reproducibility, and the C_r permutation plus oracle branch distinguishes an actual consequence association from calibration noise.

plain_motivation_en:
For a coupled future-video/action World Action Model (WAM), post-training quantization (PTQ) calibration is not only about reproducing local tensor values. A numerical intervention can change the predicted full action chunk; after the first action is executed, it can also change the simulator's next observation. The practical bottleneck is deciding which weight/activation (W/A) sites should stay at high precision when a local PTQ discrepancy does not consistently identify contact-transition consequences. OTC-PTQ therefore treats the full action chunk as an intermediate object and the one resulting control transition as the measurable boundary.

The current Phase 0 frontier makes this boundary testable. QuantWAMs (arxiv:2607.28405v1) makes joint video/action sensitivity and closed-loop protection explicit, QuantWM (arxiv:2602.02110v1) provides a distinct latent rollout/planning sensitivity branch, and Fast-WAM provides the named idm feasibility path without providing a numerical PTQ consequence signal. Together with the stated RoboTwin 2.0/LIBERO manipulation split and Fast-WAM-only staged validation budget, this supports a small one-transition diagnostic, provided the exact Optional IDM checkpoint identity is fixed in the pre-run manifest.

Several adjacent directions are already covered. QuantWAMs measures joint video/action sensitivity and repairs closed-loop protection schedules; QuantWM studies weight/activation PTQ sensitivity and long-horizon latent planning; and Fast-WAM does not provide a numerical PTQ consequence signal for one-site W/A protection allocation. Earlier task-consequence work—VAML, Model Advantage / Value-Aware Model Learning, and Deep Task-Based Quantization—already shows that downstream consequence can guide targeting, while SQIL covers critical-state protection through saliency-weighted QAT and action distillation. The narrower gap is whether one numerical W/A intervention, with every other target site at FP16, can provide a reproducible one-control-transition proxy from paired full-action-chunk and next-observation discrepancy. OTC-PTQ does not claim those broader downstream-consequence or critical-state-targeting principles as new.

If this gap closes, the field gains a bounded diagnostic for identifying when local PTQ discrepancy stops predicting one-control-transition consequence on contact states. It complements QuantWAMs' closed-loop protection branch and QuantWM's latent-planning sensitivity branch. It also enables a test of whether a C_r-ranked schedule transfers to held-out contact-sensitive failures and next-observation deviation under the same precision budget, with permutation separating the consequence association from quantizer and site-count controls. This would not establish task-loss identity, a full-horizon/replan marginal, joint-low-bit optimality, or a bytes/latency objective.
plain_motivation_zh:
对于一个耦合 future-video/action 的 World Action Model（WAM），post-training quantization（PTQ）校准不只是复现局部 tensor 数值。一次 numerical intervention 可能改变模型预测的完整 action chunk；只执行第一个 action 后，simulator 的 next observation 也可能改变。实际瓶颈是选择哪些 weight/activation（W/A）site 保持 high precision，因为 local PTQ discrepancy 并不能稳定识别 contact-transition states 上的 consequence。因此，OTC-PTQ 把完整 action chunk 当作中间对象，把随后产生的一次 control transition 作为可测量边界。

当前 Phase 0 frontier 使这个边界可以被测试。QuantWAMs（arxiv:2607.28405v1）明确处理 joint video/action sensitivity 和 closed-loop protection，QuantWM（arxiv:2602.02110v1）提供不同的 latent rollout/planning sensitivity 分支，Fast-WAM 则提供名为 idm 的 feasibility path，但没有提供 numerical PTQ consequence signal。结合已经说明的 RoboTwin 2.0/LIBERO manipulation split 和 Fast-WAM-only staged validation budget，现在可以进行一个小规模 one-transition diagnostic；前提是 pre-run manifest 中固定 exact Optional IDM checkpoint identity。

几个相邻方向已经有工作覆盖。QuantWAMs 测量 joint video/action sensitivity，并修复 closed-loop protection schedule；QuantWM 研究 weight/activation PTQ sensitivity 和 long-horizon latent planning；Fast-WAM 没有提供用于 one-site W/A protection allocation 的 numerical PTQ consequence signal。更早的 task-consequence 工作——VAML、Model Advantage / Value-Aware Model Learning 和 Deep Task-Based Quantization——已经说明 downstream consequence 可以指导 targeting；SQIL 则通过 saliency-weighted QAT 和 action distillation 覆盖 critical-state protection。因此，更窄的 gap 是：当其他 target site 全部保持 FP16 时，一次 numerical W/A intervention 能否根据 paired full-action-chunk 和 next-observation discrepancy，提供可复现的 one-control-transition proxy。OTC-PTQ 不把这些更广泛的 downstream-consequence 或 critical-state-targeting 原则宣称为新贡献。

如果这个 gap 被填补，领域将得到一个有界 diagnostic，用来识别 local PTQ discrepancy 何时不再预测 contact states 上的一次 control transition consequence。它补充 QuantWAMs 的 closed-loop protection 分支和 QuantWM 的 latent-planning sensitivity 分支。它还可以检验 C_r-ranked schedule 是否能在相同 precision budget 下迁移到 held-out contact-sensitive failures 和 next-observation deviation；permutation 可以把 consequence association 与 quantizer 和 site-count controls 区分开来。这不会证明 task-loss identity、full-horizon/replan marginal、joint-low-bit optimality 或 bytes/latency objective。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 先冻结 manifest。 在任何 paired measurement 之前，记录 calibration registry、exact checkpoint 与 configuration identities、controller/RNG/history/cache restoration contract 和 environment identity；任何必需 identity 或 restoration check 缺失或不匹配时都 halt。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 对每个 numerical weight 或 activation site r，只在 r 应用选定的 low-bit operator，其余 target site 全部保持 FP16。针对同一条 calibration record，生成与 FP16 reference 配对的 single-site low-bit branch。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 这会隔离有界的 single-site intervention，也避免把 joint coupling、joint-low-bit marginal effects 或 joint optimality 当作新的 claim。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 让匹配的 FP16 branch 与 single-site branch 生成完整 action chunks，只执行第一个 action，并记录 immediate next observation。定义 d_a(j,r)：完整 action chunk 的 MSE 除以 max(sigma_a^2, epsilon_a^2)，其中 sigma_a^2 是 D_cal 中 FP16 chunks 所有 scalar coordinates 的 population variance。定义 d_o(j,r)：next observation 的 per-pixel 绝对差除以 max(sigma_o, epsilon_o)，其中 sigma_o 是 calibration 中 per-pixel standard deviations 的 mean。使用 epsilon_a=epsilon_o=1e-3，默认 lambda_a=lambda_o=1，预注册 lambda_a/lambda_o sweep {0.5,1,2}，并将 C_r 按 episode mean 聚合，在完整 episode 上计算 bootstrap intervals；定义 L_jr 为 paired hook outputs 所有 elements 的 MSE，L_r 为其 episode mean。valid masks、observation preprocessing 与 invalid-row policy 仍须明确记录。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 这定义了一个表示 action-mediated consequence 的 one-control-transition proxy。C_r 不是 task loss、full-horizon/replan marginal，也不是 jointly-low-bit marginal。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 分别按照 C_r 和 local discrepancy 对 site 排名。将 B_site 定义为 matched local-fidelity baseline 在 preregistered manifest 中记录的 nonnegative integer high-precision-site count，并在本方法中固定 B 等价于 B_site；保护恰好 top-B_site sites，其余 site 保持 b_lo。B_site 的数值仍作为 manifest input，ties 按 registry order 处理；deployment bytes、activation workspace、scale/copy overhead 与 measured latency 必须和 site-count budget 分开记录。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 在 exact manifest 上，使用 sigma_shift_FW=1.0 运行 idm，并在指定的小规模 held-out RoboTwin 2.0/LIBERO manipulation split 上运行 infer_action；两者使用相同的 b_lo 和 B。比较两个 schedule 的 contact-sensitive task failures 与 next-observation deviation。随后在 site registry 中 permutation C_r，并使用指定的 oracle simulator-state branch 作为 positive control。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: contact-transition subset 和 permutation 是 mechanism tests：candidate 预测真实 C_r association 会带来 ranking divergence 和 transfer，而 permutation 后这个 advantage 会消失。oracle branch 用来检查 calibration noise。

plain_method_modules_en.purpose_oneline: Provide replayable calibration states and exact version and configuration boundaries for paired measurement.
Create the bounded single-site W/A intervention and compute the one-control-transition C_r signal.
Use C_r and local discrepancy to form matched protection schedules while keeping budget meanings separate.
Test contact-transition divergence and bounded transfer with permutation and oracle controls.

plain_method_modules_zh.purpose_oneline: 提供可 replay 的 calibration state，并固定 paired measurement 所需的 exact version 与 configuration boundary。
建立有界的 single-site W/A intervention，并计算 one-control-transition C_r signal。
使用 C_r 和 local discrepancy 形成 matched protection schedule，同时分开表达不同 budget 的含义。
通过 permutation 和 oracle controls 检验 contact-transition divergence 与有界 transfer。

falsification_prediction: Run the minimal experiment on the exact Fast-WAM checkpoint_FW in idm mode with sigma_shift_FW=1.0 and infer_action, using a small held-out RoboTwin 2.0/LIBERO manipulation split, the same low-bit setting b_lo, and the same high-precision budget B for local-score and C_r allocations. If the candidate works, the contact-transition subset will show a larger local-score-versus-C_r ranking divergence and the C_r schedule will reduce held-out contact-sensitive task failures and next-observation deviation relative to the matched local-score schedule, without changing the architecture or precision budget. The single load-bearing variable is C_r, the paired downstream consequence index; permute C_r across the site registry before selecting top-B sites, and the predicted effect is that the downstream contact-sensitive success/failure advantage disappears even though the quantizer and evaluation remain unchanged.
